property_summary: The owner() view returns the address stored in the dedicated ownership slot; the bug makes it return an unrelated hash value, causing a mismatch for any caller.
owner() returns the initial owner set during initialization; the bug makes it return a constant unrelated address, so the returned owner differs for any deployment.

The owner() function must always return the address stored in the OwnableUpgradeable storage slot, which is set during initialization; the bug causes it to return an unrelated keccak256-derived address, breaking equality with the actual stored owner for any deployment state.

The owner() function must return the address stored in the dedicated OwnableUpgradeable storage slot, which is set during initialization; the bug makes it return an unrelated keccak256-derived address instead, so the returned value differs from the actual stored owner for any deployment.

The paused() getter must return the same boolean value as the internal paused state that controls transfer reverts; the mutant always returns false, so after pausing, safeTransferFrom of a soul-bounded token still reverts with EnforcedPause in the original but succeeds in the mutant.

For any state, the public view paused() must return the same value as the internal pausing state that controls whether _update (and thus transfers/mints) reverts with EnforcedPause; the mutant returns false after pausing, so a subsequent transfer does not revert in the mutant while it does in the reference.

For any state, paused() must return the same value as the internal pausing state that controls whether _update (and thus transfers/mints) reverts with EnforcedPause; the mutant returns false after pausing, so a subsequent transfer does not revert in the mutant while it does in the reference.
For any state, after pausing the contract, the public view paused() must return true; the mutant always returns false, so it violates this rule after a pause.

For any unpaused state, the public view paused() must return the same boolean value as the internal pausing state that controls whether _update (and thus transfers/mints) reverts with EnforcedPause; the mutant returns false after pausing, so a subsequent transfer does not revert in the mutant while it does in the reference.
The boolean return value of paused() should reflect the actual paused state of the contract, but the mutant always returns true regardless of state.
For any caller, the paused() return value must reflect the actual internal pause state (i.e., be true only when paused), but the mutant always returns true even when the contract is not paused.
The `paused` function must return the actual stored paused state; the buggy version returns the negated value, so for any initial paused state the two contracts return opposite booleans.
The return value of paused() matches the internal paused state; the mutant inverts it, so it always returns the opposite boolean.
The return value of paused() must equal the internal paused state (true when paused, false when not); the mutant always returns the negation.
For any token id that has no specific royalty configuration, getRoyalties must return the default royaltyBPS of 500, but the mutant returns 1000.
For a token where no specific royalty is set and royalties are initialized, getRoyalties returns a RoyaltyConfiguration with royaltyBPS = 500 in the reference but 1000 in the mutant.

For any initialized contract and any token ID, a subsequent call to getRoyalties that does not revert must return a RoyaltyConfiguration whose royaltyBPS is either 500 (the default) or the customized value if one was set, but the mutant raises the default to 1000.
For any token ID, if no specific royalty is set, getRoyalties returns a royaltyBPS of 500 in the reference, but 1000 in the mutant.
For any initialized contract and any token ID, getRoyalties returns a RoyaltyConfiguration with royaltyBPS = 500 when no custom royalty is set, but the mutant returns 1000.
For any token without a custom royalty configuration, getRoyalties must return a non-zero royaltyRecipient (the default set during initialization); the mutant breaks this by returning address(0).
For any tokenId without a custom royalty config, getRoyalties must return the default royaltyRecipient set in initializeRoyalties; the bug returns address(0).
